title: I²C Environmental Sensor Pod
description: The split between what BRIEF.md fixes and what it leaves open. Every fixed_requirements entry carries the verbatim brief text that substantiates it, bound to the recorded brief digest. An open_decisions entry is a choice for the design agent: record it in 'chosen' with 'rationale', and never move it into fixed_requirements. Missing details are design freedom, not permission to fabricate unstated user requirements.

brief.authority: supplied by the benchmark; authoritative; preserved byte for byte and never edited

derivation.method: BRIEF.md was read and split; no design decision was taken. Every fixed_requirements entry, and every spec-table row sourced from the brief, carries a quotation that was checked by literal substring match against the brief bytes digested above. The build refuses to emit this file if any quotation is not found.
derivation.review: two rounds of adversarial review against the brief, looking for invented requirements, lost requirements, evidence supporting a weaker claim than the one made beside it, and worksheet questions that presuppose their own answer

fixed_requirements.requirement: The board is a compact sensor pod operating from a 3.3 V supply.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Create a compact 3.3 V I²C sensor pod measuring

fixed_requirements.requirement: It must measure four quantities: temperature, humidity, pressure and ambient light.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: measuring temperature, humidity, pressure, and ambient light.
Create a compact 3.3 V I²C sensor pod measuring temperature, humidity, pressure, and ambient light.

fixed_requirements.requirement: The host connection is a 4-pin host connector carrying 3V3, GND, SDA and SCL — four pins, those four signals. The brief neither requires nor forbids any further connector or test access beyond it.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Use a 4-pin host connector carrying 3V3, GND, SDA, and SCL

fixed_requirements.requirement: The design must include address-selection or isolation wherever it is needed so the sensors can coexist. The brief does not say whether that coexistence is on one shared bus or on segmented ones.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: include address-selection or isolation where needed so the sensors can coexist.

fixed_requirements.requirement: Heat-generating parts must be placed away from the temperature/humidity sensor.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Keep heat-generating parts away from the temperature/humidity sensor

fixed_requirements.requirement: The sensing elements must be reasonably exposed to ambient air.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: make the sensing elements reasonably exposed to ambient air.

fixed_requirements.requirement: A two-layer assembly is the stated target, consistent with the metadata's likely layer count of 2; a deviation would have to be justified and documented rather than assumed.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Target a low-cost two-layer assembly using readily available parts.

fixed_requirements.requirement: The design must target low cost and use readily available parts.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: a low-cost two-layer assembly using readily available parts.

fixed_requirements.requirement: The repository stays a consumer of the shared PCBA_AutoDesignAndTest toolkit; board-specific logic must not accumulate in the toolkit.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: The repository should remain a consumer of the shared `PCBA_AutoDesignAndTest` toolkit rather than accumulating board-specific logic in the toolkit.

fixed_requirements.requirement: Choices the brief leaves open must be made and documented as engineering decisions, not written up as if they were user requirements.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: where the brief leaves choices open, make and document reasonable engineering decisions rather than inventing hidden user requirements.

open_decisions.decision: Which sensing devices to use, and whether the four measurands come from one combined part, several parts, or some mix.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief names the quantities to measure but no sensor part, vendor or family, and no accuracy, range or resolution targets.

open_decisions.decision: How address conflicts are resolved: strap/address-select pins, an I²C multiplexer or bus switch, separate bus segments, or parts chosen to have distinct addresses.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires "address-selection or isolation where needed" but names neither the mechanism nor the devices whose addresses would collide.

open_decisions.decision: I²C pull-up resistor value, whether the pod carries them at all (versus relying on the host), and whether they are optional/depopulatable for multi-pod buses.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief fixes SDA and SCL on the connector but says nothing about pull-up location, value, or how many pods may share a bus.

open_decisions.decision: Target bus speed and the bus-capacitance / rise-time budget, including any allowance for the length of the interconnect between pod and host.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief specifies I²C but no data rate, no interconnect length and no capacitance budget.

open_decisions.decision: Connector part, body style, pitch, orientation, keying/polarisation and mating retention — and how the pod mates at all: a cable and plug, a board-to-board or mezzanine connector, or a header into a carrier.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief fixes only the pin count and the four signals; it names no connector part, footprint, ecosystem or mating style, and never says how the pod is mounted or handled.

open_decisions.decision: Pin order and numbering on the 4-pin connector.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief lists the signals as 3V3, GND, SDA, SCL but does not state that this list is the physical pin order or mandate any pinout convention.

open_decisions.decision: Whether any local regulation, filtering or reverse/miswire protection sits between the connector 3V3 pin and the sensors, or whether the rail is used directly.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief states the pod is 3.3 V and that 3V3 arrives on the connector, but is silent on conditioning that rail.

open_decisions.decision: Low-power strategy: quiescent current target, sensor duty cycling or shutdown/one-shot modes, and whether anything on the pod can be powered down.
open_decisions.why_open: Low power is a benchmark stressor in the metadata; the brief itself states no current budget, no battery or energy source, and no duty-cycle requirement.

open_decisions.decision: Decoupling scheme and any bulk capacitance at the connector entry.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief is silent on decoupling, supply impedance and transient behaviour.

open_decisions.decision: How "reasonably exposed to ambient air" is achieved: placement near a board edge, cutouts/slots, venting, keep-out zones, or conformal-coat/enclosure assumptions.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief states the goal but prescribes no mechanical means, no enclosure, and no airflow assumption.

open_decisions.decision: Optical arrangement for the ambient light sensor: which side it faces, aperture or window handling, solder-mask and silkscreen clearance, and shielding from any on-board light source.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires an ambient light measurement and general ambient exposure but says nothing about the optical path, field of view or any cover.

open_decisions.decision: The concrete thermal-separation technique and how much separation is enough: distance, copper-pour splitting, slots or thermal relief around the temperature/humidity sensor.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief says to keep heat-generating parts away from that sensor but gives no distance, no self-heating limit and no accuracy target to size the separation against.

open_decisions.decision: Board outline, dimensions, mounting holes and any keep-out for the host mechanics.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief says only "compact" and gives no dimensions, mounting scheme or enclosure interface.

open_decisions.decision: Stackup detail beyond the layer count: board thickness, copper weight, material, surface finish and soldermask/silkscreen colours.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief targets a low-cost two-layer assembly, but says nothing else about the fabrication stack.

open_decisions.decision: ESD and fault-tolerance strategy on the exposed connector lines, including hot-plug and miswire behaviour.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief mentions no protection requirement and no environment or handling model; an externally accessible host connector raises the question, but how the pod mates and is handled is itself an open choice (OPEN-05).

open_decisions.decision: Test and bring-up provisions: test points, a scan/probe access strategy, and how the assembled pod is verified against the toolkit's test flow.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief states no test, calibration or programming requirement.

open_decisions.decision: Assembly process constraints: single- versus double-sided placement, reflow profile limits, and whether any sensor forbids washing or requires post-reflow conditioning.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief asks for a low-cost assembly but names no fabricator, process or cleaning regime, and the parts that would impose those limits are not yet chosen.

open_decisions.decision: Whether any indicator LED, silkscreen labelling or identification marking is present.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief is silent on indicators and marking; if one is fitted, an LED is both a heat source and a light source relative to two of the required sensors, so it interacts with the brief's two placement constraints either way.
